rationale: Sharpening the scope of the reported defect with a source-anchored statement about which API entry points are affected, so the record distinguishes the proposal duty from the other duties of the same member. node.stepWithWaitOption routes every MsgProp through the proposal channel that the run loop's gate controls, while all other message types go to the receive channel, so the held-proposal effect cannot extend to read-index requests or to ordinary message stepping. This is recorded as behaviour knowledge with its source anchors and marked as not yet executed, with a control planned to observe a read-index completion on the same member while its proposal is held.

knowledge.statement: The proposal gate covers the MsgProp entry points of the Node API and nothing else. node.Propose, node.ProposeConfChange and node.Step with a MsgProp all end in stepWithWaitOption, which sends on n.propc, the channel the run loop only receives from while its gate variable is armed; every other message type, including MsgReadIndex, is sent on n.recvc instead. A member whose gate is disarmed therefore has its proposals and configuration proposals held, while its other duties - forwarding read-index requests to the leader it knows, answering messages and participating in replication and application - are not routed through the gate.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API run loop in this snapshot, whichever configuration flags are used, with the run loop's gate variable disarmed for the local member; statement is source-derived and has not been executed as a control.
